justification: Given the pervasive misunderstanding of what constitutes safe sanitation and how to achieve it, an important first step involved providing septic tank manufacturers with information on current Indonesian government standards for safe sanitation and the implications for their products. The Mas! partnership disseminated this information to manufacturers, leading to the local government in Bekasi certifying these suppliers as government compliant. This certification facilitated their participation in the digital platform, ensuring they could offer products that met safety standards to households.

The market analysis indicates that increasing knowledge of safe sanitation must be paired with providing households with informed sanitation options to create demand for safe sanitation. The digital platform serves as a vehicle for sales agents to deliver relevant information to potential consumers, ensuring they are aware of and have access to safe sanitation solutions.

On 30 January 2024, the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) joined seven other international press freedom organizations in a joint report after a mission to Athens in September 2023.

The report concluded that Greece is the only EU country to currently have two open cases of impunity for the murder of journalists, and almost no other country in the EU has experienced such a high number of physical attacks which endanger the safety of journalists in the last few years.

Police apprehended a man in Don Yai Hom, Nakhon Pathom, on June 8 for selling BB guns online and deceiving customers into transferring money before blocking them on Facebook to avoid contact. The suspect claimed he only took orders and did not handle deliveries. He faces charges of fraud and importing false computer data likely to cause damage. The arrest took place in front of a house in the area.

A man from Nong Han district in Udon Thani is contemplating suicide after losing 550,000 baht to an online scammer posing as an investment advisor. The scammer taunts him daily, asking if he wants to invest more. Earlier this month, Krob encountered a Facebook page promoting online sales and income generation. After expressing interest, he received a series of automated messages and a link to a Facebook account under the name Vichuda.

The mobile phones of more than 30 people in Jordan, including journalists and activists, were hacked with the Israeli-made Pegasus spyware over several years, an investigation has found.

The joint investigation, conducted by the Access Now internet advocacy group, the Citizen Lab rights group and other partners, highlighted on 1 February 2024 at least 35 cases of people who were targeted with the software, which is made by Israel’s NSO Group. Most of the cases dated from 2020 to late 2023.

The Yemeni Journalists’ Syndicate has published a report detailing media violations including attacks against journalists throughout 2023.

Violations against journalists committed by the Yemeni government accounted for 52 per cent of the 82 total recorded. 38 per cent were by the Houthi group and four per cent by media institutions. Several journalists in the country have been detained and harassed with one case of kidnapping reported.

In July 2023, an investigation by Greece’s data protection authority into the use of Predator spyware traced 350 SMS messages attempting to install surveillance software; 88 individuals were notified that their mobile phones had been targeted.

To fight stunting through integrating nutrition services into existing health facilities and strengthening healthcare workers' capacity, WHO provided training to 111 healthcare providers and nutritionists in Ngororero and Rutsiro in Rwanda on using nutrition to prevent and manage chronic diseases.

In order to build on the foundation to fight stunting, WHO trained 282 primary and secondary school teachers on health and nutrition in those same districts in order to allow them to better sensitize students and school-aged children on eating healthy.

To help people start their own businesses, Sample Uganda workshopped business models, investment options and marketing strategies with the leaders of savings and credit cooperatives. They covered skills like writing business and marketing plans, identifying funding sources, managing financial risks and estimating production costs. The workshop equipped leaders with the skills to incorporate micro aquaponics into their own business models, and to provide sustainable economic opportunities to their members.

Sample Uganda began the project to bring the technology to people living in Uganda’s urban neighbourhoods. The goal was to provide affordable, healthy food to communities and to create jobs, without putting further pressure on the environment. Sample Uganda saw aquaponics as the ideal solution. Used to grow a variety of vegetables, fruits and fish, the method employs less water than traditional agriculture and does not require the use of pesticides or herbicides.

Sample Uganda presented the benefits of the kits at market events, churches and schools, demonstrating how people could use it to start their own businesses selling the produce to their communities, in addition to the benefits of the kits, Sample Uganda  also stated that a lease-to-own option, based on the size of the kit and the customer’s ability to pay, makes the kit accessible and affordable to people from all walks of life.

Around a dozen people assaulted Esaïe Mbusa, a journalist with the privately owned radio station Venus FM, and Néhémie Paluku a correspondent with Congo 1 and the state-owned Congolese Press Agency (ACP), because they were seeking interviews with members of the local Kimbaguiste church, about the church’s dispute with a local businessman over land ownership.

The broadcast journalist Tatiana Osango was assaulted on June 5, 2024, by men said to be members of Forces of Progress, an informal youth group claiming to be associated with the ruling party Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS). They were acting on the orders of UDPS’s Secretary General Augustin Kabuya and were beating her because of her criticism of DRC President Felix Tshisekedi in an interview she hosted earlier that day with opposition politician India Omari.

On May 3, 2024, three armed soldiers with the DRC military arrived at Katoto’s home, in the Mambasa territory of the DRC’s northeast Ituri province, and told his family that they would kill the journalist for his criticism of insecurity in the territory’s Babila Babombi locality, according to a member of the journalist’s family—who was present at the time.

On February 23, at least six police officers in the capital, Kinshasa, detained and assaulted, Masand Mafuta, general director of the Culture Congo news website, confiscated his camera, dictaphone, and telephone, as well as around US$300 in cash, before releasing him the same day, according to media reports.

On February 25, 2024, three DRC armed forces soldiers attacked Lucien Lyenda, a reporter for the privately owned news website Moba Actualités Médias, as he reported on a demonstration against worsening security in the town of Kirungu in the Moba Territory of Tanganyika province.  One of the soldiers held Lyenda by the neck, and the other two punched him and hit him with rifles butts.

On December 20, 2023, the DRC held nationwide elections and supporters of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) political party—which is led by current president Felix Tshisekedi, attacked Pascal Mulegwa, a correspondent for the French broadcaster Radio France International, who was on assignment. He was punched, dragged, and thrown into a gutter, according to media reports.

On December 16, 2023, Reagean Mata Likenge, the president of the youth league of the Let’s Act for the Republic (AREP) political party in Mankanza, a town in Equateur province, ordered supporters of the party to attack Réné Mobembo, editor-in-chief of the privately owned Radio Liberté Mankanza broadcaster. The attack took place as Mobembo worked to cover the campaign of Guylain Bikoko, a legislative election candidate for the AREP political party.

Tech & Media Convergency (TMC) is involved in the USAID Digital Strategy 2024 – 2034, developed by 18 organizations as part of the Internet Governance Tanzania Working Group (IGTWG). The strategy aims to make significant impacts at national and global levels, promoting a holistic approach to digital development, with two key areas incorporated into the final document.

In parliament, Mr. Nape Nnauye highlighted the significant growth in the country's communications sector over the past year, with registered SIM cards increasing by 16.4%, mobile internet subscribers by 11.2%, and mobile money service users by 19.6%. The number of registered SIM cards rose from 62.3 million in April 2023 to 72.5 million in April 2024.

In 2022, Tanzania pledged to revolutionize education through digital initiatives at the Transforming Education Summit during the UN General Assembly. This commitment is reflected in the new education curriculum, which embraces digital literacy among students and teachers. Further to this effort, the Government has distributed 300,000 tablets to schools, demonstrating its dedication to advancing digital education.

The Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority (TCRA) is implementing a strategy to prepare digital professionals for social, economic, and digital developmental activities. One key strategy is establishing digital clubs for students and pupils at all levels, from nursery to universities.

The Ministry's 2024/25 budget aims to finalize the National ICT policy and review the Cybersecurity Act 2015. Significant infrastructure projects include 616 new communication towers in 713 wards and 636 new towers for comprehensive coverage, aiming to reach 758 in 713 wards.

For example, in the wake of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, pro-Kremlin social media accounts pushed unsubstantiated claims that Ukrainian refugees were taking advantage of welfare services in countries like Germany (Alieva, et al., 2022; Morris and Oremus, 2022).

The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) has pledged support to Tanzania in enhancing its digital transformation efforts. The partnership aims to strengthen Tanzania's digital capabilities across government and public sectors, emphasizing the importance of digital literacy for success and sustainability in today's world.

indicator: ILI3 - Vulnerability of specific groups within the context / safety and dignity of people accessing information
justification: Moen-Larsen (2020) identified security, humanitarian, integration, and nationalist frames in the analysis of Middle Eastern and North African (MENA) refugees’ representation in three Russian newspapers (Rossiiskaya Gazeta [Российскаягазета] — an official daily directly from the Russian government, Izvestiya [Известия] — a pro-government publication, and Novaya Gazeta [Новаягазета] — an opposition outlet). The overarching focus on security often painted refugees as illegal or an existential threat that could overwhelm Europe

The World Bank has provided USD 150 million to Tanzania for the Digital Tanzania Project (DTP), aiming to improve digital public services. However, the country still lacks reliable broadband services. The project aims for 75% high-speed mobile internet, 425 fast broadband facilities, and 40% online access for individuals aged 15+.

E-commerce usage in least developed countries (LDCs) increased by 140% between 2017 and 2021, but only 5.8% of individuals make online purchases compared to 62% in developed countries. Tanzania faces challenges due to inadequate ICT infrastructure, digital divides between urban and rural areas, and gender disparities.

The Eswatini Communications Commission (ESCCOM) is launching a digital literacy outreach program to promote girls in ICT. The program, part of the International Telecommunications Union's 'Girls in ICT' agenda, is being piloted at the University of Eswatini's FNB Cyberspace Computer Laboratory, with a two-day session for female pupils from Swazi National High School.

In May 2024, the TME Education programme in Zambia boosted STEM education and digital literacy through hands-on learning at Makerspace Zambia, led by ambassador Obrey Muchena. Students learned essential tech skills like soldering, programming joysticks, and controlling electronic displays. The program also introduced 3D design workshops using advanced CAD software.

Africa Endeavor 2024, a symposium aimed at enhancing cybersecurity in African armed forces, concluded its activities from July 29 to August 2, focusing on "Institutional Development - Cybersecurity Policy and Strategy Development within the Armed Forces.

Prior research has shown how not-for-profit and government organizations relied on social media to solicit donations. Also found that Nigerian refugees fleeing the war in Ukraine turned to social media to seek help, whether it was for financial aid or to find shelter.

Kaspersky, a global cyber security and anti-virus supplier, is collaborating with Zambia to combat rising cyber security threats. A delegation from Kaspersky met with the Ministry of Science and Technology to discuss their efforts both locally and internationally.

U.S. Cyber Command has deployed a team of defensive operators to Zambia for the first time since last year. The Cyber National Mission Force (CNMF) collaborated with Zambian Information Communication Technology Authority for three months in 2023 to identify network vulnerabilities and detect malicious cyber activity.

indicator: ILI3 - Vulnerability of specific groups within the context / safety and dignity of people accessing information
justification:
The study was conducted by three scientists from Toronto University analysing toxic Twitter posts concerning Ukrainian refugees for period from 24 February 2022 to 22 February 2023 with a final sample of 2,045 posts and 1,959 posts included in the analysis due to coherent coding.
The second most prevalent ones were containing expressions countering anti-refugee narratives (20 percent). These findings highlight the escalating politicization and polarization of discussions about Ukrainian refugees both online and offline. Focus was on toxic language posts.

On December 20, 2023, the Congolese media regulator, the Higher Council of Audiovisual and Communication (CSAC), called and ordered a technician from the privately-owned television company Bleusat to cut the programming signal of Perfect Télévision in Kinshasa, according to media reports. The order originated from Perfect Télévision’s reports on polling stations not opening on time and missing electoral kits at several voting centres in Kinshasa and across the country.

A freelance reporter John Kanyunyu Kyota, told the Committee to Protect Journalists, that he has received at least four death threats from anonymous callers purporting to be members of DRC intelligence agents since November 22, 2023. Kanyunyu has worked for the German broadcaster Deutsche Welle in the country’s Beni city and runs a WhatsApp group called “Habari Moto Moto,” a forum for local political news.

On November 28, Desis Koyo, the mayor of the Mongala province’s capital, Lisala, issued an order banning all programs of the private Radio Top Lisala broadcaster for “incitement to hatred and serious harm to the process current election in the DRC,” according to Koyo who spoke on the phone with CPJ and director of this media Ernest Ngasa who spoke with CPJ.

On December 9, around 20 supporters of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS), Tshisekedi’s political party, attacked and punched Mao Zigabe, a correspondent with the privately owned television broadcaster Digital Congo, at a hotel in Goma, the capital of North Kivu province, according to media reports.

On October 20, 2023, an officer with the National Intelligence Agency (ANR) arrested Blaise Mabala, radio coordinator with the privately owned Même Morale FM and correspondent with the privately owned website okapinews.net, and detained him at a military camp in Inongo, capital of the western Mai-Ndombe Province, according to Okapinews.net and a member of the Union Nationale de la Presse du Congo.

subindicator: ILS4.4 - Deliberate communication shutdowns / restrictions from malicious actors
justification: The mayor of the northwestern Congolese city of Lisala, Desi Koyo, issued an order, indefinitely suspending broadcasts by Radio Top Lisala, on October 6, 2023. The order said that the station had defied the mayor’s August reporting ban on Moleka for using “insolent, immoral and defamatory” language on the current affairs program Tic Tac which undermined the dignity of Mongala Province authorities.

On Friday, September 8, around 10:30 p.m., two Congolese national police officers arrested Bujakera, a reporter for the privately owned Jeune Afrique news website and Reuters, as well as deputy director of publication for the local news website Actualite.cd, at the N’djili international airport in Kinshasa, the capital, according to a report from the privately owned Le Congo Libere news website.

On Friday, September 1, Soleil Ntumba Mufike was filming police carrying out the court-ordered eviction of the family of the deputy director of the national agency Direction General of Migration, in the provincial capital, Kananga, when Luhizon Zigabe, the director of that agency, ordered around 10 immigration officers to stop the journalist from recording. The immigration officers grabbed his clothes, dragged him, and threw him to the ground.

Kuzikesa, a presenter and general manager of privately owned CML13TV, said on Facebook that he was in transit to the Congolese capital, Kinshasa, when a dozen men dressed in civilian clothes, who identified themselves as security officers for Tshisekedi, attacked him and snatched his two phones and hand luggage.

subindicator: ILS4.4 - Deliberate communication shutdowns / restrictions from malicious actors
justification: On May 22, 2023, the DRC’s media regulator, Conseil Supérieur de l’Audiovisuel et de la Communication (CSAC), banned Kuzikesa from working as a journalist for 72 days and ordered a 45-day suspension of CML13TV’s broadcast signal.

As noted in the Security Service of Ukraine, the Russian special services will try to use the situation in the Kursk region to baselessly accuse the Ukrainian military of committing war crimes. This is due to the fact that the Russian military cannot effectively resist the offensive actions of the Ukrainian side.

At the same time, Andrii Kovalenko, head of the Center for Combating Disinformation, clarified that the Russian side is already spreading fakes about the alleged killing of civilians by the Ukrainian military in the Kursk region, looting and more.

"Russian propaganda will make great efforts to create scenes of alleged war crimes in Suja and other places in the Kursk region with the help of fakes," he added.

indicator: ILI3 - Vulnerability of specific groups within the context / safety and dignity of people accessing information
justification: Head of the Committee of the Verkhovna Rada on the Organization of State Power, Local Self-Government, Regional Development and Urban Planning Olena Shulyak added that among the indicators that show the existence of a discrimination problem in Ukraine the widespread cases of sexism in advertising, offensive statements based on the patriarchal model of society regarding women, including from representatives of the state authorities, are already traditionally mentioned.

CERT-UA has detected a massive distribution of malicious emails allegedly on behalf of the SBU. More than 100 computers, including government agencies, have been infected. The emails contain a link to a file with the ANONVNC virus.

On July 25, 2023, Lich Nkele, the federal president of the Movement for the Liberation of the Congo (MLC), a party allied with President Felix Tshisekedi, and three MLC militants assaulted José Nkoso, director of the privately owned Radio Bomoko Mankanza, at his home in Mankanza town in northwestern Equateur province, according to José Nkoso, who spoke to the Committee to Protect Journalists.

On Saturday, July 29, Frank Kalonji, a reporter with the private news website Actu7.cd, told CPJ that an unknown number of supporters of leading opposition presidential candidate Martin Fayulu—who claimed to have won DRC’s 2018 presidential elections but lost a court case challenging the result—slapped and manhandled him and snatched his phone to prevent him reporting on their Engagement for Citizenship and Development (ECIDé) party’s rally in the capital, Kinshasa.

On Saturday, July 29, opposition presidential candidate Delly Sesanga of the Envol party and five reporters were assaulted while trying to attend a rally in Kananga, the capital of Kasaï-Central province, according to one of the reporters, Elysée Odia of the private news site Yabisonews.cd, who spoke to the Committee to Protect Journalists via messaging app.

The M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka ordered four private broadcasters — Radio Horizon FM, Radio Communautaire de Rutshuru, Radio Alliance, and Radio Racove — to stop carrying the program “Sauti ya Wahami” (Voice of the Displaced) for 60 days in the “interest of consolidating peace, the communion of communities and promoting living together.”

On  June 28, 2023, at least 12 soldiers from the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) arrested, punched, and used belts to hit Ngoyi, a reporter with the U.N.-backed Radio Okapi; Malou, a reporter with state-owned Radio Télévision Nationale Congolaise (RTNC); and Nkelani, a camera operator in training with the state-owned broadcaster RTNC2. The three journalists had been covering a land dispute in Kinshasa, the capital, according to a report.

On Saturday, May 20, a group of protesters at a rally organized by opposition presidential candidates in Kinshasa, the capital, attacked Djokwa while she covered demonstrators clashing with police, according to media reports.

On Friday, April 14, three Congolese National Intelligence Agency (ANR) agents arrested Gustave Bakuka, a reporter with the privately owned broadcaster Radio Mushauri, at his home in Kindu, the capital of DRC’s eastern Maniema province, according to a tweet by Kindu-based journalist Grace Mbambi and another local journalist who spoke to CPJ by phone.

On April 10, 2023, a prosecutor in the capital, Kinshasa, summoned and detained Kayiba, a reporter with the privately owned broadcaster Kin Actu TV and privately owned news website Reportage.cd, in connection to two tweets, according to a report by privately owned news website Actungolo and Kayiba’s lawyer, who spoke to CPJ by phone and messaging app.

On April 9, 2023, Jean-Calvin Mingashanga, the elected representative for the central city of Tshikapa, sent an audio message to Sylvain Kabongo, a reporter with the privately owned Netic-news.net, and threatened him with arrest for publishing a “baseless article,” according to a report by his outlet and Kabongo, who spoke to the Committee to Protect Journalists.

On April 2, 2023, a group of about 12 police officers arrested Tshibangu, director of the privately owned online broadcaster Chat Television, while he was driving in Kinshasa, the capital, according to the journalist, who spoke to the Committee to Protect Journalists via messaging app.

On March 27, 2023, three officers with the National Intelligence Agency arrested Ngongo, director of Radiotélévision Evangélique Phare (RTEP) broadcaster, in the city of Kindu in the eastern province of Maniema, according to two local journalists familiar with the situation who spoke to the Committee to Protect Journalists.

The minister of communication and media for Lomami province, Pascal Ernest Mulumba Kalende, ordered Radio Tokomi Wapi to suspend its operations and close its office in the provincial capital of Kabinda until further notice, according to those sources.

Crime Insight review about humanitarian and protection risks in Brazil derived from crime points out that with the rise of online banking in Brazil, stealing money can now more easily be done remotely as criminals convince victims to transfer cash or sensitive information by phone or email. This has led to virtual crimes becoming increasingly common in Brazil, even as other types of crime drop.

subindicator: ILS2.2 - Accessible, safe and accurate information
justification: According to OCHA, GBV awareness-raising activities reached 686 beneficiaries (108 girls aged 5 to 17, 100 boys aged 5 to 17, 86 women aged 18 to 59, and 49 men aged 18 to 59). The aim was to educate communities on protection issues, enhancing their knowledge and awareness to foster a safer environment.

In prioritizing the safety and welfare of children during disasters, the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) in the Cagayan Valley trained local government representatives on establishing and managing Child-Friendly Spaces (CFS) in evacuation centers.

The head of the DRC’s National Intelligence Agency (ANR), Yangoba Katanga Yangozo, invited Sylvain Kiomba editor-in-chief of the Shilo FM, for questioning on January 5 and detained him when he appeared at Yangoba’s office in the city of Lubao. Joseph Ebondo, reporter at the Shilo FM, told CPJ that he was detained later on January 5, when he went to Yangoba’s office to seek information about Kiomba’s status.

On October 25, 2022, Bono Emakitshi, administrator of the Lodji territory in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s central Sankuru province, issued a directive suspending the operations of privately owned broadcasters Radio Losanganya headed by François Lendo, and Radio Grand Tam-tam which is equally headed by Jean-Paul Osongo.

On Wednesday, November 16, two police officers arrested Makambu, program director of community broadcaster Radio Communautaire pour le Renouveau du Kwango (RCRK), from his home in Kenge in the country’s northwest, and later took him to the Kenge central prison, according to a report by local press freedom group Journaliste en Danger (JED).

On the morning of Tuesday, November 8, the DRC’s immigration authorities, the Direction Générale des Migrations (DGM), summoned and expelled Rolley, a French reporter for Reuters, according to reports by Reuters as well as tweets by the U.N. human rights office in the DRC. Rolley had received DGM permission to cover a climate conference in Kinshasa, the capital, in October, while she waited for a separate accreditation, it was not approved which led to her expulsion by the authorities.

On October 20, 2022, Janvier Bamunoba, a camera operator with the privately owned Buniaactualité TV broadcaster, was at the airport in Bunia, the capital of eastern Ituri province, to cover the return of musician J-Five Matete, who had recently won a competition in the capital Kinshasa, when police officers detained him, according to Bamunoba, who spoke to CPJ by phone, and news reports.

On October 20, 2022, when David Ramazani arrived at the airport in Bunia, three DRC armed forces soldiers in uniforms of the Republican Guard stopped him, refused to let him enter, slapped him, punched him in his face, and threatened to whip him if he continued to advocate for his colleague’s release, according to Ramazani and a video of the incident taken by another journalist.

On Saturday, October 29, at least 23 journalists from Kiwanja and Rutshuru took refuge at the Kiwanja headquarters of the U.N. mission in the DRC, known as MONUSCO, following the takeover of the cities by the M23 rebel group and threats to kill local journalists. Two members of MONUSCO working in Kuwanja, who spoke to CPJ said, the U.N. has since evacuated the 23 journalists to Goma, the nearby capital city of North Kivu province, via flights.

On October 19, four Congolese military intelligence agents arrested and detained Christophe Katembo Muthahinga, a reporter with local broadcaster Radio du Peuple Oicha, on a roadway between the capital of Ituri province, Bunia, and the eastern city of Oicha while he photographed a traffic jam and interviewed drivers according to Katembo and Issa Musango, director of Radio du Peuple Oicha.

On September 19, the Kinshasa Gombe Peace Court sentenced Gauthier Sey Tshiang, director of the privately owned online media outlet Netic News, to one year in prison for damaging imputations, or making statements to harm an individual’s reputation, spreading false rumours, and fraud over his reporting on Jean Simon Mfuti Kiaku, acting director of the DRC’s National Social Security Fund. The court also ordered Sey to pay US$10,000 in damages to Mfuti, who brought the case against the journalist.

On September 17, 2022, Jules Lodi Emongo, governor of Sankuru province, ordered privately owned radio stations based in the province’s Lomela city—Radio Ekitela, Radio Numbampela, and Radio Liberté Sankuru—to stop broadcasting until further notice, according to a press release from the Sankuru provincial government.

Bakhchysaray district court in Crimea refused to transfer political prisoner Marlen Asanov from colony in Republic of Mordovia.  A civilian journalist and former entrepreneur sentenced to 19 years in prison for "organization of terrorist activities" and preparation for "forcible seizure of power" wanted to move closer to family.

Marlen Asanov among other things has been helping families of political prisoners since 2014 and published videos on YouTube documenting violations by the Russian forces in Crimea.

A fake page allegedly belonging to the Red Cross of Ukraine was created on the Telegram social network. Administrators ask people to provide personal information to receive financial assistance. The fake channel "Red Cross of Ukraine" duplicates most of the news from the official channel of the Ukrainian Red Cross, the organization writes. Administrators of the fake channel encourage people to leave their personal data in an online application in order to allegedly receive UAH 6,500 in monetary support.

22 Chinese nationals and one Cameroonian have been sentenced to seven to eleven years in prison and fines for cybercrime in Zambia, according to AP News.

The Committee to Protect Journalists has called on Mozambique's northern Cabo Delgado province officials to withdraw accusations of journalists colluding with terrorists and publishing false news, and to allow media freedom.

The Committee to Protect Journalists has called on Mozambican authorities to investigate the harassment and assault of at least five journalists covering election-related events since March and take immediate steps to ensure the press can report on crucial public matters.

The Mozambican chapter of MISA has expressed concern over the emergence of threats against journalists covering the conflict in Cabo Delgado. The provincial governor, Valige Tauabo, has accused journalists of collaborating with Islamic terrorists in the province, causing concern among the regional press freedom body.

CPJ has assisted at least 30 Ethiopian journalists and media workers who have been exiled since 2020, with most fleeing to neighboring African countries and a few in Europe and North America. In May and June 2024, CPJ interviewed some of these exiled journalists about their experiences.

Belete, along with numerous other Ethiopian journalists, has been forced into exile due to harassment and persecution in a country where the government has a strong media control. CPJ has documented repression and exile linked to reporting on events like protests after the 2005 election and censorship of independent media and bloggers.

Belete, along with numerous other Ethiopian journalists, has been forced into exile due to harassment and persecution in a country where the government has a strong media control. CPJ has documented repression and exile linked to reporting on events like protests after the 2005 election and censorship of independent media and bloggers.

Ethiopia is experiencing a significant increase in its online community due to rapid internet usage expansion and social media adoption. As of 2023, the country had 20.86 million internet users, with 6.4 million actively engaged on social media.

indicator: ILI3 - Vulnerability of specific groups within the context / safety and dignity of people accessing information
justification: The Amhara people in Ethiopia are facing ongoing struggles against oppressive regimes, including the Abiy regime, which has been accused of genocide and spreading hate speech, highlighting their long-standing struggle for survival.

subindicator: ILS2.2 - Accessible, safe and accurate information
justification: According to UNICEF, A total of 2,456 (872 girls, 417 boys, 721 women and 446 men) received Gender-Based Violence (GBV) risk mitigation, prevention and response interventions in the same counties affected by drought and refugee camps through capacity building, individual case management, access to safe spaces for survivors and those at risk.

subindicator: ILS2.2 - Accessible, safe and accurate information
justification: In order to ensure learning continuity at the time of emergencies, 679 governmental officials (482 men and 197 women) were trained on preparedness and response planning, effective coordination, Disaster Risk Reduction and Resilience building.

indicator: ILI3 - Vulnerability of specific groups within the context / safety and dignity of people accessing information
justification: Due to stigmatization, fear of reprisals, harmful social norms, the absence or lack of access to services, impunity and safety concerns, sexual violence continued to be vastly underreported. And therefore, the numbers reported may not fully capture the prevalence of cases of sexual violence against children that may have occurred in north-east Nigeria.

The IFRC is set to bolster media relations and content gathering initiatives by creating and disseminating communication materials and resources. These efforts will be shared on platforms like Facebook and Twitter to propagate advocacy messages both globally and regionally. Additionally, the IFRC will aid in mitigating reputational risks at the national level and will ensure that Movement actors present a unified voice, thereby building trust among partners, donors, and other stakeholders.

subindicator: ILS2.2 - Accessible, safe and accurate information
justification: In the ongoing fight against GBV, UNHCR and its partners conducted several sensitization workshops in May, reaching a total of 1,317 individuals. These workshops aimed to raise awareness on various GBV-related topics and the available services, with participants including women (34%), men (31%), girls (27%), and boys (8%).

subindicator: ILS2.2 - Accessible, safe and accurate information
justification: According to UNHCR, In refugee camps, there were additional workshops that focused on educating girls about the menstrual cycle, sexual exploitation, and harassment. Additionally, sensitization sessions for mixed couples (refugees and host community members) were also held, addressing peaceful cohabitation and the consequences of physical and emotional violence.

subindicator: ILS2.2 - Accessible, safe and accurate information
justification: A 4-day training course was organized for 14 teachers (10F and 04G) from pre-schools in refugee camps, with the support of the Ngozi provincial director of education and recommendations were made aimed at facilitating the inclusion in the Burundian education system.

French journalist Antoine Galindo, a reporter for Africa Intelligence, was detained by Ethiopian security forces on February 22, wearing civilian clothing, according to his employer. The incident occurred during a reporting assignment in Ethiopia.

Ethiopian Satellite Network TV (ESAN TV) is concerned about YouTube's arbitrary suspension of a prominent Ethiopian channel, which has nearly half a million subscribers. ESAN TV notes a pattern of selectively suspending Ethiopian channels critical of the Abiy regime without providing an explanation, citing "community guidelines violations".

Ethiopian media workers face imprisonment with beatings, interrogations, solitary confinement, visitation rights violations, sexual abuse, and denied sanitary products. Upon release, threats threaten censorship or complete halt of work.

The 2020-2022 Tigray civil war and the 2023 Amhara conflict have led to a swift return to a harsh media environment, characterized by arbitrary detentions and the expulsion of international journalists.

The Mozambican authorities must conduct a thorough, impartial investigation into the arbitrary arrest of journalist Sheila, as seen in videos supplied to Amnesty International and shared on social media. Adriano Nuvunga, the president of the RMDDH, emphasized the need for a fair trial and the prosecution of the perpetrators.

subindicator: ILS2.1 - Telecommunications infrastructures damage or limitations
justification: Internet connectivity in Mozambique and other African countries experienced significant disruptions due to failures in SEACOM and EASSy submarine cable systems, crucial for network infrastructure.

subindicator: ILS4.4 - Deliberate communication shutdowns / restrictions from malicious actors
justification: Ethio-Telecom, Ethiopia's government telecom provider, has presented a report to Parliament stating that the internet service restrictions imposed in the country extend beyond its jurisdiction, causing economic loss and deprivation of citizens' rights, which could negatively impact the country's image.

subindicator: ILS4.4 - Deliberate communication shutdowns / restrictions from malicious actors
justification: The Amhara region is facing significant challenges due to internet blackouts, fuel scarcity, and transport disruptions, which are posing significant challenges for public and humanitarian agencies. The federal government's restriction of access to mobile and fixed-lined internet and social media platforms has been met with condemnation from human rights advocates.

subindicator: ILS4.4 - Deliberate communication shutdowns / restrictions from malicious actors
justification: Since the state of emergency took effect, the Amhara region has been under a command post led by the head of the National Intelligence and Security Service, reporting directly to the prime minister. The government has limited access to information through internet bans and communication blackouts.

subindicator: ILS4.4 - Deliberate communication shutdowns / restrictions from malicious actors
justification: NetBlocks' 2023 report reveals Ethiopia ranks second in income loss after Russia due to a significant internet shutdown, following a global monitoring of internet services. The deliberate internet shutdown by the government is believed to have multifaceted motivations, including suppressing protests, restricting freedom of expression, and safeguarding election processes.

Local journalists are facing challenges in covering the conflict in Cabo Delgado, where the Mozambican government, with support from the Southern African Development Community and Rwanda, is fighting an insurgency by Islamic State-linked militia. Challenges include lack of timely authorities' responses to journalistic queries and security force attacks.

A resident of Myrnograd, Donetsk region, who works as a truck driver, was informed of the suspicion of spreading information of a military nature. According to the prosecutor's office, in July, a member of the pro-Russian group in the Telegram messenger sent information of a military nature to the "DPR People's Militia" bot(this name is slur using by Russian propagandists, the correct notion will be "part of Donetsk oblast controlled by Russian government") — he sent text messages twice.

The general director of the occupying media holding "Krym Television and Radio Company" was sentenced to 12 years in prison with confiscation of property under four articles of the Criminal Code of Ukraine, including for collaborationism. 
It is said that he was involved in propagandist informational activities, provided by the occupying authorities, as well as disseminate information about forcibly changes of Ukrainian borders.

Analysts of the Armed Forces of Lithuania recorded in July the increase in informational pressure from Russia and Belarus directed against the country, especially in the field of defense. According to the Lithuanian military, 312 information cases were detected last month, more than 200 of them related to the defense sector.
In particular, the Baltic Connection 24 (BALTCON24) exercise with the deployment of Patriot air defense systems was presented as preparation for aggression.

indicator: ILI3 - Vulnerability of specific groups within the context / safety and dignity of people accessing information
justification:
On August 1, Russia withdrew from the Framework Convention of the Council of Europe on the Protection of National Minorities.

The convention, signed in February 1995, establishes the basic principles of treatment of national minorities in Europe, including the prohibition of their discrimination and forced assimilation, the freedom to practice one's religion and to speak freely in one's native language.

subindicator: ILS2.2 - Accessible, safe and accurate information
justification:
The Ministry of Education and Science made changes to the Standard Educational Program for students in grades 5-9. Now schools will be able to change the curriculum if necessary, using the reserve of additional hours.

"Now the educational process will become more flexible, various curricula and variable courses will increase, and special attention will be paid to overcoming educational losses," the ministry claims.

The suspects in the murder of Aidos Sadykov, a Kazakhstani journalist, could have worked in the National Security Committee and the Foreign Intelligence Service of Kazakhstan. Meiram Karataev and Altai Zhakanbaev are suspected in the murder occured on 18 June in Kyiv.
Aidos Sadykov was engaged in oppositional movements firstly as a politic then as journalist. After 2014 after publication of his wife`s material concerning public procurement back in Kazakhstan earned a political asylum and lived in Kyiv with his family.

The Security Service reported another suspicion of crimes against the national security of the "mouthpiece" of Russian propaganda Volodymyr Rohov.

The former active participant in creation of Russian proxy "Novorossia" now positions himself as a "military expert" and publicly justifies the war of the Russian Federation against Ukraine and the war crimes of the Russian troops.

With the beginning of the large-scale invasion, Rohov "re-profiled" himself as a propagandist, and actively participates in information diversions against Ukraine, especially on his Telegram channel.
